body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the application. By this Response, claims 1-2 and 19-20 have been amended. No new matter is added by these amendments, which are supported by the Applicant's specification as filed, e.g. paragraphs [00198], [00206], [00255]-[00257] and [00265]. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims in view of the remarks presented below.
Claims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as allegedly being indefinite.
By this Response, Applicant has amended claims 1 and 19-20 to address the 112 rejections, taking into consideration the comments and suggestions in the Office Action.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the 112 rejections on claims 1-20 be withdrawn.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Liu et al.

("Tracking Vital Signs During Sleep Leveraging Off-the-shelf WiFi"; hereinafter "Liu"), in view of Xu et al. ("Attention-based Walking Gait and Direction Recognition in Wi-Fi Networks"; hereinafter "Xu"), and further in view of Suyambukesan et al. (US2006/0077306; hereinafter "Suyambukesan").
Applicant respectfully traverses each of the above rejections, and does not agree on any Official Notice taken in the Office Action.
Without agreeing on the above rejections and solely for expediting the allowance of the
application, independent claim 1 is amended to recite among other things:
obtaining a time series of channel information (CI) of the wireless channel based
on the received wireless signal, wherein each CI is a vector associated with a time
stamp with N components,
computing a time series of denoised CI (DCI) by denoising the time series of CI
(TSCI), wherein each DCI is a vector associated with a time stamp with N
components,
computing a time series of concatenated CI (TSCCI) based on a
concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI (TSDCI), wherein:
each concatenated CI (CCI) associated with a respective time stamp is a vector comprising 2N components and is computed by concatenating a
respective CI associated with the same respective time stamp and a
respective DCI associated with the same respective time stamp
corresponding to the respective CI,
a first set of N components among the 2N components are associated with the respective CI, each of the N components in the first set being
associated with a respective component of the respective CI,
a second set of N components among the 2N components are associated with the respective DCI, each of the N components in the second
set being associated with a respective component of the respective DCI,
computing a one dimensional (1D) characteristic function of CCI of the TSCCI in
a sliding time window,
computing a two dimensional (2D) decomposition of the TSCCI based on the 1D
characteristic function in the sliding time window,
enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a vertical highpass horizontal lowpass
filtering, and
monitoring the periodic motion of the vital sign based on the enhanced 2D
decomposition.
(Emphasis added.)
The Office Action correctly noted that Liu does not disclose "computing a time series of
concatenated CI (TSCCI) based on a concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI
(TSDCI)," as recited in claim 1. The Office Action then relied on Xu to teach these features.
See, Office Action, pp. 4-5. Xu performed CSI denoising using a Butterworth bandpass filter
with upper and lower cutoff frequency being 90Hz and 5Hz respectively. See, Xu, pp. 5-6. But
after denoising the CSI, Xu did not re-use the original CSI that is not denoised. Xu failed to
use BOTH the original CSI and the denoised CSI together. In particular, Xu failed to teach or suggest a concatenation of the original CSI and the denoised CSI.

In contrast, as required by Claim 1, after CI is denoised to generate DCI, the original CI continues to be used to form CCI, by concatenating the original CI with the DCI. In particular, Claim 1 requires that a N-dimensional original CI vector is concatenated with a N-dimensional DCI vector to form a 2N-dimensional CCI vector.

Although Xu mentioned "[b]y concatenating the first-order derivative, namely the first- order difference, of the primary profile, the proposed method gets a 384xT dimensional walking profile for each CSI stream," this concatenation in Xu is different from the concatenation in the amended claim 1. See, Xu, p. 7. First, Xu stacked several "PCA components" computed from denoised CSI "to form the primary walking profile with dimensions 192xT for each PCA component, where T is the length of the spectrogram (i.e., the amount of chunks)". Id. These PCA components in Xu are different from original CSI and denoised CSI. The T chunks of data in Xu are stacked with a different time stamp, rather than concatenating the original CSI and the denoised CSI at the same time stamp. Then, Xu concatenated first-order derivative of these "PCA components," which is also totally different from concatenating the original CSI and the denoised CSI. Id.

As such, Xu does not teach or suggest: "computing a time series of concatenated CI (TSCCI) based on a concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI (TSDCI), wherein: each concatenated CI (CCI) associated with a respective time stamp is a vector comprising 2N components and is computed by concatenating a respective CI associated with the same respective time stamp and a respective DCI associated with the same respective time stamp corresponding to the respective CI, a first set of N components among the 2N components are

associated with the respective CI, each of the N components in the first set being associated with a respective component of the respective CI, a second set of N components among the 2N components are associated with the respective DCI, each of the N components in the second set being associated with a respective component of the respective DCI," as recited in the amended claim 1.

In addition, the Office Action correctly noted that Liu does not disclose "enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a [non-separable] vertical highpass horizontal lowpass filtering," as recited in claim 1. The Office Action then relied on Suyambukesan to teach these features. See, Office Action, p. 5. Suyambukesan applied a vertical high pass filter followed by a horizontal low pass filter to a video frame for a display device. See, Suyambukesan, [0028]. But the 2D decomposition of the TSCCI in Claim 1 is vastly different from video frames to a person with ordinary skill in the art (POSITA). While a vertical highpass horizontal lowpass filter can preserve horizontal lines and remove lines in other direction (e.g. vertical lines), such horizontal lines are common in video frames because of the many horizontal edges of tables, chairs, wall, floor, etc. But it was NOT well-known to POSITA that such line structures in video frames would also occur in the 2D decomposition of the TSCCI in Claim 1. Thus, there was no motivation for a POSITA to apply the vertical highpass filter and the horizontal lowpass filter of Suyambukesan to the 2D decomposition of the TSCCI in Claim 1.

It is well settled that establishing a prima facie case of obviousness requires that all claim limitations recited in a claim must be taught or suggested by the prior art. MPEP §2143.03. Clearly, taken individually or in combination, the cited references do not pass this test. Thus, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with respect to claim 1. Thus, claim 1 is patentable.
Claims 2-18 depend from claim 1, and are thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 1, and for the additional features recited therein.

Independent claims 19-20 have amended to include similar features as claim 1, and are thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 1, and for the additional features recited therein.
In view of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 are overcome and should be withdrawn.
No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.

In view of the above, each of the presently pending claims in this application is believed to be in immediate condition for allowance. Accordingly, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw the outstanding rejection of the claims and to pass this application to issue.
